source.text: Archaeological discovery shows that "Nanjing Man" lived in more than 500 thousand years ago. Zun, a kind of wine vessel, was found to exist in Beiyinyangying culture of Nanjing in about 5000 years ago. In the late period of Shang dynasty, Taibo of Zhou came to Jiangnan and established Wu state, and the first stop is in Nanjing area according to some historians based on discoveries in Taowu and Hushu culture. According to legend,[which?] Fuchai, King of the State of Wu, founded a fort named Yecheng (冶城) in today's Nanjing area in 495 BC. Later in 473 BC, the State of Yue conquered Wu and constructed the fort of Yuecheng (越城) on the outskirts of the present-day Zhonghua Gate. In 333 BC, after eliminating the State of Yue, the State of Chu built Jinling Yi (金陵邑) in the western part of present-day Nanjing. It was renamed Moling (秣陵) during reign of Qin Shi Huang. Since then, the city experienced destruction and renewal many times.[citation needed] The area was successively part of Kuaiji, Zhang and Danyang prefectures in Qin and Han dynasty, and part of Yangzhou region which was established as the nation's 13 supervisory and administrative regions in the 5th year of Yuanfeng in Han dynasty (106 BC). Nanjing was later the capital city of Danyang Prefecture, and had been the capital city of Yangzhou for about 400 years from late Han to early Tang.
source.title: Nanjing

source.text: Yaxing Coach (Yangzhou Yaxing Motor Coach Co., Ltd) is a bus manufacturer based in Yangzhou, Jiangsu, China. It is a subsidiary of Jiangsu Yaxing that was founded in 1998. Buses are produced under the "Yaxing", "Yangtse（Yangzlv）", and more recently Asiastar brands.
source.title: Yaxing Coach

source.text: China Sunergy () is a Chinese solar cell products manufacturer based in Nanjing, Jiangsu. The company specializes in creating solar cells from silicon wafers. China Sunergy has a major customer base in China, but also sells their products internationally. On May 17 2007 the company began producing both monocrystalline and multicrystalline silicon solar cells. In 2012 the annual production of the cells were 1 GW and PV modules 1.2 GW. After listing as a NASDAQ Company in 2007, in 2013 May 23 China Sunergy opened its first international manufacturing base in Turkey. Turkey factory has the biggest solar cell and module capacity among both in Turkey and Europe. CSUN currently is the only Chinese solar cells and module manufacturer with a manufacturing base in Europe. Located in Tuzla Free Trade Zone, Istanbul, CSUN (Turkey) is in progress of building its second factory in Turkey within 2015. CSUN has been recognized as a Tier 1 module supplier by the Bloomberg New Energy Finance (BENF) PV Module Maker Tiering System on 23 March 2014.
source.title: China Sunergy

EXPERIMENT TASK — WRITE SPARQL FOR MUSIQUE QUESTION

Prompt version: musique-sparql-evidence-first-v1

ROLE

You are constructing the SPARQL computation for a multi-hop question-answering
experiment over a frozen RDF graph.

Your job is not merely to state or force the expected answer.

Your job is to express a query whose ?answer value is obtained by executing
graph patterns against the RDF graph supplied below.

WHY THE QUERY STRUCTURE MATTERS

The query is executed over the frozen graph.

After execution, the computation is traced backwards to determine which RDF
statements contributed to each returned answer, and those RDF statements are
resolved back to their exact source occurrences.

Therefore the answer must genuinely arise from graph matching.

A query that simply injects an already-known answer may return the right value,
but it does not express the computation we need to observe.

THE FROZEN GRAPH IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THIS TASK

Every triple pattern you rely on must correspond to relations actually available
in the frozen RDF graph.

Do not invent a relation because it would make the reasoning chain work.

Do not assume a benchmark relation exists unless you can locate the corresponding
RDF triple in the supplied graph.

If the graph does not contain the relation needed for an intended reasoning
step, do not fabricate it.

DECOMPOSITION

The MuSiQue decomposition describes the intended semantic dependency of the
question.

Use it to understand what each reasoning step means and to look for corresponding
relations in the frozen graph.

The decomposition does not create facts in the graph.

An intermediate answer from the decomposition may help you recognize entities,
but the SPARQL computation must still derive its bindings through the graph
relations that actually exist.

CONSTRUCT THE QUERY

Find the RDF triples in the frozen graph that can realize the question.

Use variables to connect dependent graph patterns.

The final ?answer variable must occur in an RDF triple pattern that retrieves
its value from the graph.

Example:

Graph:
    <Organization> <abbreviatedAs> <FIFA> .

To retrieve the organization represented by FIFA:

    ?answer <abbreviatedAs> <FIFA> .

Do not instead write:

    <Organization> <abbreviatedAs> <FIFA> .
    BIND(<Organization> AS ?answer)

The first query derives the answer.
The second query inserts an answer that was already known.

SUPPORTED QUERY FORM

Use a SELECT query with ?answer as the answer variable.

Use basic RDF triple patterns and joins through shared variables.

Do not use:
- BIND
- VALUES
- SELECT DISTINCT
- GRAPH
- SERVICE
- SPARQL updates
- FROM clauses

Python adds dataset scoping after your semantic query is produced.

MATCHED TRIPLES

matched_triples is your record of the exact frozen-graph statements you relied
on while constructing the query.

Copy those N-Triples lines exactly from the supplied frozen graph.

Do not report a triple that is not present in the graph.

matched_triples describes your evidence selection; the SPARQL query describes
the computation you construct from that evidence.

OUTPUT

Return only valid JSON:

{
  "matched_triples": [
    "<subject> <predicate> <object> ."
  ],
  "sparql": "SELECT ?answer WHERE { ... }"
}
